newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian opposition chief wins parliament seat.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian opposition chief wins parliament seat.

text.p: Tanzania's chief opposition leader Augustine Mrema was on Tuesday declared winner of a parliamentary by-election in the capital Dar es Salaam.

Mrema, an anti-corruption campaigner, stood against Abdul Cisco Mtire of the ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM-Party for the Revolution) for Temeke seat, vacant since CCM parliamentarian Ramadhani Kihiyo resigned due to poor health three months ago.

Mtire, a little-known civil servant, received backing from President Benjamin Mkapa, cabinet ministers and other political heavyweights in more than two months of campaigning for Sunday's poll. Mrema polled 54,840 votes versus Mtire's 33,133.
The National Electoral Commission said the vote was fair.

CCM now has 217 seats and opposition parties have 58 seats in the 275-member parliament. Mrema was the main opposition candidate against Mkapa in a presidential election last year and took 27.8 percent of votes against the victor's 61.8 percent.
Mrema, a former interior minister and deputy prime minister heads the main NCCR-Mageuzi opposition party.
